### DEV/project_memsearch-index-path-drift.md

---
name: memsearch-index-path-drift
description: "the SessionEnd memsearch hook read its path config from a Windows-era ~/Desktop/DEV path and silently fell back, indexing 4 of 10 memory paths for months after the Mac migration"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  modified: 2026-08-15T04:07:30.329Z
  originSessionId: 75381393-88b6-4b65-960d-6613e08f7060
---

`~/DEV/KeystoneOS/data/memory-index-paths.json` is the single source of truth for which directories memsearch indexes. Three writers read it: the SessionEnd hook `~/.claude/hooks/memsearch-sync.js`, `~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1` (nightly; 09:00 since 2026-08-29), and the Codex hook `KeystoneOS/scripts/codex-hooks/memsearch-sync.ps1`.

**Found 2026-08-14:** the JS hook pointed at `~/Desktop/DEV/KeystoneOS/data/memory-index-paths.json` — the pre-migration Windows layout. DEV lives at `~/DEV` on this Mac, so the read threw, the `catch` returned a hardcoded fallback, and the hook indexed **4 paths instead of 10** for months. The fallback itself was also stale (`~/Desktop/SecondBrain/...`, which does not exist since the vault move). `daily-backup.ps1` used `$U/DEV` and was already correct; the Codex hook self-locates from its own script path and was fine. So only the JS hook drifted — and it is the one wired into `settings.json` (`SessionEnd`, 50s timeout).

Unindexed as a result: `SecondBrain/Knowledge`, `SecondBrain/Inbox/meetings`, `SecondBrain/morning-briefings`, the Mac memory slug `-Users-kristinarash-DEV/memory`, `KeystoneOS/decisions`, `.codex/memories`. Incremental recall for all of those depended entirely on that nightly.

**Why:** the failure mode was invisible. A silent `catch → fallback` means a migration-broken config path degrades into a quieter, smaller, still-succeeding job — no error, no log line, no failed run. Nothing surfaces until someone asks "why didn't that turn up in search?" The bug was not the wrong path; it was that the wrong path cost nothing to have.

**How to apply:**
- Any config-file fallback in this stack must log to `.errors.log` when it fires. The JS hook now does. A fallback that never announces itself is a silent outage with a long tail.
- When auditing post-migration breakage, grep for `Desktop/DEV` and `Desktop/SecondBrain` — those two strings mark Windows-era assumptions. Do not trust that a script "works" as evidence its paths resolved; check what it actually resolved to.
- Verify path config by resolving it in isolation (`node -e` reading the same JSON, printing EXISTS/MISSING per entry) rather than by running the indexer — that proves the fix without taking the Milvus Lite write lock.
- Paths in the JSON that do not exist yet are harmless; every writer filters through an existence check before passing them to memsearch.

**There were TWO copies of this hook, and fixing one did not fix the other (2026-08-15).** A Codex review found `~/.codex/hooks.json` wires its *own* copy at `~/.codex/hooks/memsearch-sync.js`, separate from the Claude copy at `~/.claude/hooks/memsearch-sync.js`. The Claude copy was repaired 2026-08-14; the Codex copy still pointed at `~/Desktop/DEV/...`, so **every Codex session-end indexed a stale 5-path fallback** that also referenced the old `~/Desktop/SecondBrain` — missing SecondBrain/Knowledge, Inbox/meetings, morning-briefings, KeystoneOS decisions and the Mac memory slug. Now fixed and verified resolving all 11 configured paths.

Ordering trap in that repair: `const ERR_LOG` was declared *after* `const PATHS = resolvePaths()`. Adding a `logErr()` call inside `resolvePaths` therefore hit the const temporal dead zone, and `logErr`'s own `try/catch` swallowed the ReferenceError — reproducing the silent fallback the fix was meant to remove. `ERR_LOG` must be declared before `PATHS`.

**How to apply:** when fixing a hook, first ask *which copy the harness actually wires* — check `~/.codex/hooks.json` and `~/.claude/settings.json`, not just the file you happened to open. Grep the whole home tree for the hook's basename before assuming there is one.

**A THIRD hook had the same stale path, found 2026-09-01 during `/doctor-plus`.** `~/.claude/hooks/keystone-unified-snapshot.js` (SessionStart) read `~/Desktop/DEV/KeystoneOS/outputs/dashboard/unified-snapshot.md`, threw ENOENT, and its `catch (_) { emit(null) }` injected **nothing at all** — for every session since the migration. The snapshot file was being written correctly the whole time at `~/DEV/KeystoneOS/outputs/dashboard/`; only the reader was wrong. Zero symptoms: no error, no log, valid JSON on stdout, session starts normally.

The 2026-08-14/15 sweep fixed the two `memsearch-sync.js` copies but did not catch this one, so **"grep for `Desktop/DEV`" must cover every file in `~/.claude/hooks/` and `~/.codex/hooks/`, not only the hook currently being repaired.** Run it as a sweep across the whole hooks tree, not per-file.

That sweep then found a **fourth** copy — `~/.codex/hooks/keystone-unified-snapshot.js`, byte-identical and wired in `~/.codex/hooks.json`. Also fixed 2026-09-01.

**A second signature the `Desktop/DEV` grep cannot catch:** `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` (dated 2026-08-08) had been through a bad `claude` to `Codex` find-replace, so it told Codex to read `~/.Codex/global-memory/`, `~/.Codex/projects/<slug>/memory/` and `~/.Codex/Codex-memory-compiler/daily/` — none of which exist. Grep for `.Codex` (capital C) as well as `Desktop/DEV` when auditing migration damage. Also check which AGENTS.md the harness actually reads: `~/.claude/AGENTS.md` was correct but referenced by nothing.

Resolved 2026-09-01: `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` is now a symlink to `~/.claude/AGENTS.md`, so the pair has one home and cannot drift again. `setup-agents-symlinks.sh` was also sourcing `CLAUDE.md` for that link — the one thing `CLAUDE.md` explicitly forbids — and now sources `AGENTS.md`. Running that script used to recreate the bug.

Repaired 2026-09-01: path corrected to `~/DEV`, required sources now push a visible "SessionStart hook could not read a required memory file" block into `additionalContext` instead of failing silently, and the hook now also injects `global-memory/USER.md` + `MEMORY.md` (replacing a prose rule in `CLAUDE.md` that nothing enforced). The KeystoneOS snapshot is pointed at, not pasted.

### DEV/project_milvus-lock-misdiagnosis.md

---
name: milvus-lock-misdiagnosis
description: milvus-lite reports lock contention as a version-incompatibility error; following its advice destroys a working memsearch index for hours
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa062f93-2c55-4016-b9c6-f1a32e0a7083
  modified: 2026-08-15T02:42:26.304Z
---

When memsearch fails to open `~/.memsearch/milvus.db`, milvus-lite prints:

> Failed to open the local Milvus Lite database. If this database was created with an older Milvus Lite release, it may not be compatible with Milvus Lite 3.x. Move the existing .db file aside, then rebuild the index...

**That text is a generic open-failure string, not a version verdict.** It fires just as readily on plain lock contention. Diagnosed 2026-08-14: the underlying error was `BlockingIOError: [Errno 35]` from `flock`, and `lsof +D ~/.memsearch/milvus.db` named the holder — a concurrent manual `memsearch index` running after the SecondBrain vault move. The same DB with the same milvus-lite 3.1.1 had indexed successfully hours earlier.

(Attribution caution: at the time this was written the holder was assumed to be "another Claude session," inferred from an unfamiliar PID and shell-snapshot id. Eric corrected that — it was not. `lsof` tells you *which process*, never *which agent or person*; state the process and leave the actor unnamed.)

**Why:** following the message's advice (move the .db aside, rebuild) throws away a working index and costs an hours-scale re-index of the SecondBrain library — a self-inflicted outage in response to a transient collision.

**How to apply:**
- Before believing any milvus-lite "incompatible database" message, run `lsof +D ~/.memsearch/milvus.db` and `ps aux | grep memsearch`. A live holder means wait, not rebuild.
- Milvus Lite is single-writer. `daily-backup.ps1`'s advisory lock (`.memsearch-index.lock`, ~line 416) coordinates the nightly reindex with the SessionEnd hook only — it cannot see a hand-run `memsearch index`, so manual indexing during a backup window collides. Avoid running `memsearch index` by hand while the nightly backup may fire.
- `memsearch-index:full-set` in `.errors.log` is therefore usually transient. Confirm the lock is free, then let the next scheduled run clear it.

**Tooling mitigation added 2026-08-14 (because the written warning was not enough).** Later the same day a session ran `memsearch reset --yes` anyway and triggered a ~2h full rebuild — the exact outage this note warns about, with the note already on disk. Prose guidance does not survive contact with a scary error message, so the guard is now in code:

- `~/.local/bin/ms-search` — lock-aware retry wrapper for reads (`search` / `stats` / `expand` / `transcript`; write subcommands are refused). Retries with backoff to 60s (`MS_SEARCH_MAX_WAIT`), then exits **75** saying the DB is healthy and not to run `reset`. It retries **only** on `DataDirLockedError` / `another process holds the lock` / `Resource temporarily unavailable` / `_acquire_lock` / `fcntl.flock`; it deliberately does **not** key on the "may not be compatible with Milvus Lite 3.x" sentence, since that same wording is emitted for genuine incompatibility — so real corruption still fails fast and passes its exit code through.
- `~/.claude/hooks/memsearch-sync.js` now classifies those same lock signatures as transient instead of escalating them as hard errors. Caveat: `bumpTransientStreak` shares one counter across all transient classes at threshold 6, so a cluster of session-ends during a long rebuild can still escalate — downgraded, not eliminated.

**How to apply (updated):** prefer `ms-search "query"` over `memsearch search` for recall; it waits out a busy index instead of surfacing the misleading message. Reserve bare `memsearch` for writes.

Related: [[backup-sync-system]] (carries the earlier two-writer lesson), [[memsearch-index-path-drift]] (the config drift found while fixing this), [[drive-fuse-rsync-mtime-loop]]

The morning-briefing project was **retired 2026-08-14** at Eric's request — he wasn't using it and it was overhead the system had to manage. He may approach the idea differently in future.

What was done:
- `com.keystone.morningbriefing` (7:20 AM) booted out and `disabled`; **plist retained** at `~/Library/LaunchAgents/`. Do not confuse it with `com.keystone.morning` (6:00 AM KeystoneOS `morning-cadence`), which is unrelated and still live.
- `~/DEV/morning-briefing/` deleted (338 MB — mostly a 305 MB `.venv` and a 32 MB authenticated Outlook browser profile). Code is intact at `github.com/erash11/morning-briefing` (0 unpushed commits at removal).
- Local `secrets/` destroyed (Outlook `owa-profile`, `gmail_credentials.json`, `gmail_token.json`) plus `~/.config/morning-briefing/`. Outlook auth had already lapsed; briefs were emailing 0 threads.
- **`KeystoneOS/data/jobs.json` entry removed — this is the one that actually mattered.** Disabling launchd was not enough: the entry had `reconcile: true` / `maxAttemptsPerDay: 2`, and `keystone-reconcile.ps1` (which dot-sources `run-ledger.ps1`, reading `data/jobs.json` live) re-launched the briefing at 19:39 on 2026-08-14 *despite* launchd being disabled — logged as `MAKE-UP morning-briefing`. Its `authWarnProbe` is also what wrote the "Outlook auth expired / run reauth.sh" line into `.errors.log`. When retiring any KeystoneOS job, remove the `jobs.json` entry or the reconciler resurrects it.
- Lost in the removal (accepted): uncommitted `config.toml` edits from 19:37 that day, and `logs/` (508 KB, 113 run logs). Briefing *outputs* were in the vault; run logs were not.
- Dropped from `backup-manifest.json`, stack-doctor checks, and `CREDENTIALS.md` (which had a stale **OUTSTANDING** `GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD` item, now moot).
- KeystoneOS: brief moved to `projects/retired/morning_briefing.md`, `registry.md` + `data/projects.json` marked Retired.

**Why it matters:** the 56 briefings at `~/SecondBrain/morning-briefings/` were **kept**, added to the memsearch index set, and **verified retrievable** 2026-08-15 (916 chunks indexed; queries like "Matt Tardif Firstbeat intro" and "FORMS TASKS OWED timecard Playfly" return `morning-briefings/*.md`). Note recall needs *specific* terms — generic queries like "meetings to schedule" rank other sources above them. 42 of them carry synthesized digests (who asked for what, meetings to schedule, tasks owed) spanning 2026-05-22 → 08-14. ### DEV/project_path-shadowing-and-cleanup.md

---
name: path-shadowing-and-cleanup
description: "PATH shadowing repair 2026-08-13 — measure PATH with env -i, grep hardcoded paths before deleting a binary, broken symlinks evade find -type f"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

---

Repairs made 2026-08-13 on this Mac, and the four traps hit doing it. All four generalise.

**What was wrong and is now fixed:**
- `uv` existed twice — `~/.local/bin/uv` 0.11.6 (Apr) shadowed Homebrew's 0.12.1 (Jul), so a
  three-month-old build was winning. Fixed with `uv self update` → 0.12.3, then `brew uninstall uv`.
- PATH had duplicate `~/go/bin` and `~/.local/bin` entries (17 entries → 15). Sources: a redundant
  export in `.zshrc`, a duplicated `go/bin` line, and two unguarded `brew shellenv` calls in `.zprofile`.
- An entire pre-migration Node install at `/usr/local` (~690 MB: node, npm, npx, corepack, stale
  codex/gemini/gws) removed. `/usr/local/bin` now holds only Docker Desktop + kubectl.
- `FIREFLIES_API_KEY` moved from plaintext in `.zshrc` into the login Keychain.

**The four traps — these are the reusable part:**

1. **A PATH read from inside a tool shell is a lie.** Any earlier `export PATH=…` in the session
   pollutes it. This produced a wrong claim (`~/.bun/bin` reported as duplicated when it was not).
   Honest measurement:
   `env -i HOME="$HOME" USER="$USER" TERM=xterm SHELL=/bin/zsh /bin/zsh -lic 'echo $PATH'`
2. **PATH order only governs lookups by name.** Deleting `~/.local/bin/uv` would have silently
   killed three hooks in `~/.claude/settings.json` (SessionStart/PreCompact/SessionEnd) that call
   the memory-compiler by *absolute path*. Always `grep -rl '/full/path' ~/.claude ~/DEV` first.
3. **Scheduled jobs are the blind spot.** Eight KeystoneOS launchd agents referenced `/usr/local`
   — harmlessly, as PATH entries — but nothing in shell config would have shown them. Check
   `~/Library/LaunchAgents` before touching a shared prefix.
4. **`[ -e ]` and `find -type f` both skip broken symlinks.** 92 npm man pages were symlinks into
   a just-deleted tree; the first cleanup pass removed 1 of 92 and reported success. Use
   `find … \( -type l -o -type f \) -delete`.

**Still open (his action):** rotate the Fireflies key — the old value persists in two `.zshrc`
backups, session transcripts, and `~/.claude/file-history/`; the Keychain does not retract those.
Also `sudo rm -rf /usr/local/include/node` (62 MB) and `sudo rmdir /usr/local/lib/node_modules`.

**Why:** each of these cost real debugging time, and three of them fail *silently* — the wrong
version runs, the hook stops, the file never gets deleted, with no error.
**How to apply:** before asserting where a tool lives or deleting any binary on this machine, run
the `env -i` measurement and the hardcoded-path grep. See also [[zsh-shell-traps]] and
[[terminal-fluency-workspace]].

### DEV/project_printing-press-spec-traps.md

---
name: printing-press-spec-traps
description: "Spec-authoring and pipeline traps discovered printing catapult + zotero CLIs (Aug 2026) — pagination params, envelope-nested fields, probe fixtures"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: a86cfb00-e6d1-46b9-8cdc-35e21acd9931
  modified: 2026-08-06T23:21:52.213Z
---

Traps hit while printing `catapult-openfield-connect` and `zotero-research-library` (2026-08-05/06), each cost a debugging cycle:

- **Offset pagination MUST name `cursor_param`** in the spec (e.g. `cursor_param: start` for Zotero). Omitted, the generator defaults to `after`; servers that ignore unknown params return page 1 forever while the cursor climbs (silent infinite loop, same 25 rows).
- **Envelope-nested APIs leave all extracted store columns empty.** Zotero items nest fields under `$.data.*`; the store's `LookupFieldValue` reads top-level keys only, so title/date_added/name columns are NULL. Hand commands must read `json_extract("data", '$.data.<field>')` and search via `resources_fts` (joins on its `id` column — NEVER on rowid, which is hashed).
- **Novel command names collide with framework commands** (`search`, `periods`) — validate-narrative catches it late; check the framework command list at absorb time. Renamed to `ground`.
- **Dogfood probes run with PP_DOGFOOD=1** which curtails syncs to one page — happy-args fixtures must resolve against a ~25-row cache. Use dynamic specials (`top`, `last`) instead of baked keys.
- **`pp:happy-args` grammar**: positional labels need angle brackets (`<query>=hamstring`); `--flag=value` tokens pass flags; probes time out at 30s so unbounded commands need a bounding flag in happy-args.
- **generate --force preserves hand files but re-emits generated docs** — keep a `fix-generated-docs.py` per run to strip phantom "Covered paths" bullets after every regen.
- **Novel child commands must use direct `cmd.AddCommand(newXxxCmd(...))` calls.** The public library's SKILL.md verifier discovers subcommands by regex-scanning for that exact pattern; any helper indirection (e.g. `addNovelCommandIfAbsent`) hides children and their flags, failing CI on doc examples. Guard with a `hasSubcommandNamed` check instead of wrapping AddCommand.
- **Zotero /deleted returns a category map** (collections/items/searches/tags/settings arrays in one object), not a list — generic extractors keep only `items` and silently drop the rest; flatten all categories into keyed tombstones.
- **Catapult API v6**: date filter on POST /stats hangs server-side — express windows as activity_id sets; `requested_only=false` needed for athlete/activity/date columns; dates arrive MM/DD/YYYY.
- Related: [[zsh-shell-traps]]

### DEV/project_s2-cognition-analysis.md

---
name: s2-cognition-analysis
description: "S2 Cognition data traps (vendor reference group, P/K short battery, invalid reports) and the standing rule that any flagging threshold must be null-calibrated and pre-registered before the data is touched"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

  originSessionId: 856bd54e-8db3-42f5-a770-103ee081614e
  modified: 2026-08-16T18:37:34.242Z
---

S2 Cognition analysis lives at `~/DEV/S2_Evaluation` (private repo `erash11/S2_Evaluation`). V1 shipped 2026-08-16 with a **null finding**: no offensive lineman is cognitively atypical once the flagging threshold is calibrated against a null model.

**Vendor data traps** (learned the hard way, not documented by S2):

- Percentiles are scored against **"NFL PROSPECTS - ALL POSITIONS"**, not a college or position-specific reference group. So a percentile is only comparable *within* that reference group — cross-position pooling is legitimate (Baylor rooms range 42nd–82nd), but "50th percentile" does not mean "average for his position."
- The **P/K battery has only 7 measures**, not the usual 9, with zero N/A cells. That is structural to the vendor's short battery, not a parse bug — don't chase it.
- Some reports fail S2's own **validity check**; the vendor marks them INVALID. Exclude them from analysis and surface as a retest recommendation instead of silently dropping.
- Test years are mixed across a roster. Flag the year as a diagnostic; don't filter on it.

**Standing methodological rule** (ADR 0013, applies beyond S2): never set a "flag the outlier" threshold without first simulating what a **pure-noise room** produces at that threshold. The original 1.5 SD rule flagged 10 of 15 linemen; a homogeneous null room flags 7–13 of 15, so the rule was measuring nothing. Related: with 9 categories, max-over-N inflation makes almost any naive threshold vacuous.

Corollary — because Eric is his own reviewer on side-lane projects, thresholds get **pre-registered in a timestamped git commit before the data is on the machine**. Changing a threshold after seeing results requires a new ADR stating what was wrong; never retune silently.

### DEV/project_settings-json-bom-trap.md

---
name: settings-json-bom-trap
description: "A bad Windows write to ~/.claude config files does TWO things at once — adds a UTF-8 BOM (dcg then reports the hook as missing) and CP1252-double-encodes every non-ASCII character (statusline bars turn to junk). Check settings.json, CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md, and check for both faults."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 7741462f-dac7-4551-8692-76574bbfd202
  modified: 2026-09-12T03:37:42.609Z
---

One bad write from the Windows machine damages `~/.claude` config files in
**two independent ways**. They arrive together and are fixed together, but they
surface at completely different times, so finding one does not mean you found
both. On 2026-09-10 only the BOM was caught; the mojibake sat undetected for two
more days until the statusline was looked at directly on 2026-09-11.

## Fault 1 — the UTF-8 BOM (loud, misleading)

`~/.claude/settings.json` acquires a **UTF-8 BOM** — the 3 invisible bytes
`EF BB BF` at the start. Claude Code parses the file anyway, so nothing in
Claude Code looks broken. `dcg` (Destructive Command Guard) does not, so it
prints at every session start:

```
[dcg] Hook missing from ~/.claude/settings.json — run: dcg install
```

**The message is wrong, and its suggested fix is the wrong fix.** The hook was
present and correct all along. Running `dcg install` would have added a second
hook to a file the tool cannot read.

**Diagnose, don't trust the banner.** `dcg doctor` names the real fault:

```
Checking hook wiring... ERROR
  Invalid JSON: expected value at line 1 column 1
```

"Line 1 column 1" on a file that is visibly valid JSON means a BOM.

## Fault 2 — CP1252 double-encoding (silent, cosmetic-looking)

The same write reads the file's UTF-8 bytes as **CP1252**, then saves them back
as UTF-8. Every non-ASCII character becomes 2–3 junk characters. Nothing errors.
Nothing warns. JSON stays valid. You only notice by *looking at rendered output*.

The statusline is where it shows, because it is the only config that draws
box characters:

| Intended | Becomes | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `░` U+2591 | `â–‘` | statusline meter bar (empty) |
| `▓` U+2593 | `â–“` | statusline meter bar (filled) |
| `↑ ↓ →` | `â†‘ â†“ â†’` | git ahead/behind, cache arrow |
| `—` em-dash | `â€”` | CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md prose |
| `…` `’` `·` | `â€¦` `â€™` `Â·` | CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md prose |

The `â` prefix is the tell — it is `0xE2`, the first byte of most UTF-8 symbols,
read as Latin-1.

## It is not only settings.json

The 2026-09-11 sweep found the damage in **three** files. Two of them also
carried BOMs that the 9/10 fix never looked at:

- `~/.claude/settings.json` — 113 mangled chars (no BOM by then, already fixed)
- `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` — 8 mangled chars **+ BOM**
- `~/.claude/AGENTS.md` — 25 mangled chars **+ BOM**

Always sweep the whole tree, never just the file that complained.

## Fix — strip BOM, then reverse the encoding, then verify rendering

```python
import json
p = "/Users/kristinarash/.claude/settings.json"
s = open(p, encoding="utf-8").read().lstrip("﻿")
fixed = s.encode("cp1252").decode("utf-8")   # exact inverse
json.loads(fixed)                             # must still parse
open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n").write(fixed)
```

`.encode("cp1252")` raising means the file is only *partly* mangled, or a BOM is
still present — strip the BOM first, and never force the round-trip on a file
where it fails. Sweep for survivors by scanning for these patterns:

```python
pats = ['â–‘','â–“','â†‘','â†“','â†’','â€”','â€™','â€¦','Â·']
```

**Verify the statusline by rendering it**, not by reading the JSON — pipe a
sample payload into the `statusLine.command` and look at the bars.

Writing the repaired file needs the Write tool, not a shell heredoc: `dcg`
blocks any truncating `>` redirect into `~` (`core.filesystem:redirect-truncate-root-home`).

## The generalisation

Two tolerant readers hid this for two days. Claude Code tolerates the BOM, so
the statusline kept running; the terminal tolerates mojibake, so it kept drawing
*something*. **The strict reader complains about the wrong thing (`dcg`), and the
cosmetic damage never complains at all.** When a config file has been touched by
the other machine, check the first bytes *and* grep for `â` — one fault does not
imply the other has been handled.

Related: [[dcg-guard-blocks]], [[hook-two-copies-trap]], [[github-consolidation]],
[[path-shadowing-and-cleanup]]

| `.jsonl` sessions scanned | 414 |
| Distinct real skills **ever** invoked | **58** |
| Used 3+ times | 30 |
| Used exactly once | 19 |

Everything is global. That is the anti-pattern, not the achievement.

## The rule that fixes it — promotion

**Everything stays project-level until it earns global.** A skill lives in
`<project>/.claude/skills/` until it proves itself across 2+ projects, then it
gets promoted to `~/.claude/skills/`. Keeps the global load small and the blast
radius tight — so when something underperforms you can tell a *model* problem
from a *harness* problem from an *organisation* problem.

## The audit question

Not "how often did I run this skill?" but **"would the model do this fine without
the skill now?"** A skill is a crutch; as the brain gets smarter the crutch starts
to *limit* it. Seasonal skills (`forecast-capture`) and occasional ones
(`ingest-book`) are low-count by design — low usage alone is not a delete signal.

## Re-measure (BUILTIN filter is the whole trick)

Without the `BUILTIN` set you also count `/exit`, `/clear`, `/compact` and friends,
which inflates the total to 74 and buries the real skills.

```bash
python3 - <<'EOF'
import glob,re,collections
BUILTIN={'exit','clear','compact','rename','color','login','logout','plugin','doctor',
'help','model','config','resume','cost','status','init','agents','mcp','hooks','memory',
'review','vim','terminal-setup','install-github-app','add-dir','bug','release-notes',
'pr-comments','ide','permissions','statusline','output-style','todos','export',
'privacy-settings','upgrade','fast','artifacts','tasks','loop','context','usage','rewind',
'sandbox','feedback','worktrees','skills','reload-skills','reload-plugins','bashes',
'keybindings','theme'}
c=collections.Counter()
for f in glob.glob('/Users/kristinarash/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl',recursive=True):
    try:
        for line in open(f,encoding='utf-8',errors='ignore'):
            if 'Skill' not in line and 'command-name' not in line: continue
            for m in re.finditer(r'"name"\s*:\s*"Skill"\s*,\s*"input"\s*:\s*\{[^}]*?"skill"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"', line):
                c[m.group(1)]+=1
            for m in re.finditer(r'<command-name>/([a-zA-Z0-9:_-]+)</command-name>', line):
                c[m.group(1)]+=1
    except Exception: pass
real={k:v for k,v in c.items() if k.split(':')[-1] not in BUILTIN and k not in BUILTIN}
print("distinct real skills ever invoked:",len(real))
print("used >=3 times:",len([k for k,v in real.items() if v>=3]))
print("used exactly once:",len([k for k,v in real.items() if v==1]))
for k,v in sorted(real.items(),key=lambda x:-x[1]): print(f"{v:5d}  {k}")
EOF
```

## Decision, 2026-09-12

**Do the skill audit BEFORE adopting Pi** (`pi.dev`) as an alternative harness.
Rationale: the leverage is the bloat, not the harness. Auditing first means any
future harness move ports ~30 good skills instead of ~200 mixed ones.

Pi facts, verified from `pi.dev/docs/latest` 2026-09-12 — full note at
`~/SecondBrain/Inbox/2026-09-12-pi-harness-research.md`:

1. **No sandbox, no approval flows.** "Pi does not include a built-in sandbox."
   Project trust only guards resource *loading*, not what the agent then does.
   Never run Pi in `~/DEV` or near `DexaProject`. Trial it in `~/pi-trial` or a
   container (`sbx` keeps the credential off the container).
2. **Skills port for one line.** Pi implements the Agent Skills standard and already
   auto-discovers `~/.agents/skills/` — where 45 of the skills live. Add the rest with
   `{"skills": ["~/.claude/skills"]}` in `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`. It loads
   `AGENTS.md` **or** `CLAUDE.md` directly.
3. **Hooks → TypeScript extensions is a bounded port, not a rewrite** (earlier note
   said "weeks", that was wrong). Hooks here are already `.ts`; Pi's `tool_call` event
   returns `{block, reason}` — the same shape as the dcg guard.
4. **Claude subscription through Pi bills per token as "extra usage", NOT against plan
   limits.** Changes the economics of brain-swapping.

Config lives in `~/.pi/agent/` and survives npm uninstall.
See also [[hook-two-copies-trap]] and [[dcg-guard-blocks]].

## Audit outcome, 2026-09-12

**Both tiers executed.** 99 skills archived, global **160 → 61**, roster cost
**19,158 → 6,428 tokens/session (a 66% cut)**. Zero regressions: none of the 99
had ever been invoked in 414 sessions.

Decision 2026-09-12: keep the `mattpocock-skills` and `superpowers` **plugins** and
archive the local bare-name duplicates. The plugin (v1.2.3, 35 skills) ships every
duplicate removed and is newer than the July symlinks. Rule that follows: when a
plugin and a local skill share a name, **the plugin wins** — delete the local copy.

Script: `~/.claude/skills-audit-2026-09-12.sh` (archives, never deletes — undo with
`mv ~/.claude/skills-archive/2026-09-12/* ~/.claude/skills/`).
Report: `~/SecondBrain/Inbox/2026-09-12-skill-audit.md`.

Traps found while doing it:
1. **CORRECTED 2026-09-12 — `~/.claude/skills/` IS version-controlled.** It is its own
   git repo, remote `https://github.com/erash11/claude-skills.git`, and the audit was
   committed as `3ab4467 chore: apply global skill audit` and pushed. The earlier note
   that it is "gitignored, archive is the only undo" was true only of the *`dotclaude`*
   repo, which ignores this path — a different thing. **Git IS the safety net here, and
   it is also how the cut reaches Windows.** Undo with
   `git -C ~/.claude/skills revert <sha> && git push`, not the archive folder
   (`skills-archive/` is not in the repo and never reaches the other machine).
2. **A cut in `~/.claude/skills/` does NOT reach `~/.agents/skills/`.** After the audit,
   98 of the 99 archived skills were still live in the pool (306 entries there vs 61
   canonical). Claude Code stopped seeing them; **Pi auto-discovers that folder**, so
   installing Pi would have re-exposed all of them. Always cut both.
3. **Skills live in three places and it is easy to edit the wrong copy.**
   `~/.claude/skills/` (19 entries were symlinks pointing *out* to the pool),
   `~/.agents/skills/` (Pi, Cowork), `~/.codex/skills/` (Codex, 27 symlinks + 5 real
   dirs). Count with `find -L`; plain `find` undercounts.
4. **`sync-to-codex.sh` did `rm -rf "$dst/$s"; cp -R "$SRC/$s"`** over a 7-name
   allowlist. If `$SRC/$s` ever became a symlink into `$dst`, that deletes the real
   data. `dev-sync` tells you to run it after every pull. A `.ps1` twin has the same
   shape — patch both.
5. **`~/.claude/skills/_shared/`** holds `config.json` + `Inference/` and is resolved by
   10+ skills via `parents[2]/_shared/config.json`. It has **no SKILL.md**. Never treat
   "no SKILL.md" as "orphan, delete".
6. **"606 plugin skills" is cache, not load.** Only 6 of 24 plugins are enabled
   (~37 skills exposed). The rest are disabled plugins and old cached versions.

## Executed 2026-09-12 — traps the live run found

- **Views are live links now.** `~/.agents/skills/<owned>` and `~/.codex/skills/<owned>`
  point into canonical, so anything that writes a view path writes canonical
  (`graphify install --platform agents` does; see [[graphify-runtime-setup]]).
- **`skillOverrides` in `~/.claude/settings.json` breaks parity silently.** Codex and Pi
  ignore that file, so an owned skill set `"off"` there is hidden in Claude Code but live
  elsewhere. Perfect frontmatter does not help; `skill-portability-check.py` fails it.
  Resolved 2026-09-13: Eric re-enabled the 7 (ArXiv, ISA, Science, capture-insight,
  library-review, pp-espn, session-miner) — `~/.claude` commit `21c686d`, checker 42/42.
  Never set an owned skill "off" again; retire it from canonical instead.
- **Git's spelling wins, not the Mac's.** APFS is case-insensitive: the folder showed
  `Harvest` while git recorded `harvest/`. Check `git ls-files` before "fixing" a
  name to match the disk.
- **A `closeout` in another session commits your uncommitted work** (it swept Task 5's
  34 SKILL.md edits into its own commit). Commit each verified step immediately.
- **Description budget:** keep each description under ~650 chars; Claude Code caps the
  combined listing.

## Architecture decided 2026-09-12 (executed through Task 5 the same day)

**Canonical = `~/.claude/skills/`** (the git repo, real directories only, **never commit
a symlink** — Windows pulls this repo). `~/.agents/skills/` and `~/.codex/skills/` are
**generated views**, rebuilt by `sync-to-codex.sh` from a complete manifest of every
canonical dir holding a SKILL.md, recorded in a `.generated-by-sync-to-codex` ownership
file so an audit can tell a generated entry from a third-party `npx skills add` install.
Symlink on Mac, copy on Windows.

Portable frontmatter contract (fires in Claude Code *and* Codex): `name` must equal the
directory name (TitleCase is legal), and `description` needs **both** a positive
"Use when …" clause with literal trigger phrases *and* a negative "Do not use …" clause.
Codex reads only `name` + `description` (+ optional `metadata.short-description`) and
ignores `argument-hint` / `allowed-tools`. Codex over-fires without the negative clause;
Claude will not trigger without the literal phrases.

Plan (Codex-approved after 6 review rounds, 10→0 findings):
`~/DEV/KeystoneOS/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-12-harness-agnostic-aios.md`.
See [[dev-layout-and-discovery]], [[hook-two-copies-trap]], [[vendored-skill-install]].

## Listing trim, 2026-09-14 (doctor-plus)

**40 owned skills are `"name-only"` in `~/.claude/settings.json` `skillOverrides`**
(dotclaude commit `172d547`). 13 stay full: the ones Claude invoked itself 2+ times
(memory-write, CreateSkill, impeccable, claude-stack-doctor, codex-review, name-meetings,
project, graphify, fireflies-intake, html-to-pdf, meeting-prep, status-report) plus
sports-science-research-grounding. Chosen from the usage scan above (model calls vs typed).

- Why `name-only`, not `"off"` or `disable-model-invocation`: the name stays listed, so
  Skill-tool chains (`startup`→`dev-sync`, `weekly-review`→`meeting-sync`) still work,
  the portability checker only fails `"off"`, and Codex/Pi still see full descriptions.
- Cost: those 40 fire less on phrases ("goodnight", "capture this"). Type `/name`.
- Next-session check: if ~17 local skills still show as bare names, the listing budget
  is being eaten by plugin skills, not these. Promote a skill back to `"on"` by deleting
  its line.

### DEV/project_vendored-skill-install.md

---
name: vendored-skill-install
description: "Installing a third-party skill so Claude Code, Codex and Cowork can all use it — the canonical store, the two symlinks, the CLI flag trap, and why Cowork is different"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: a6dfb3da-c339-44b1-a836-2a6884e07ea6
  modified: 2026-09-04T13:43:21.110Z
---

Third-party skills live in **`~/.agents/skills/<name>/`** (the real files, ~360 of
them) with `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` as the install ledger. Both harness
directories are symlinks into it:

- `~/.claude/skills/<name>` → `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (relative)
- `~/.codex/skills/<name>` → `~/.claude/skills/<name>` (absolute, hopping through
  the Claude symlink — verified on disk 2026-09-04. It does **not** point straight
  at `~/.agents/skills/`.)

Install with the CLI that owns that store when you can:

```bash
npx -y skills@latest add <owner>/<repo> -g -a claude-code -a codex -s <skill> -y
```

**Trap: in Claude Code auto mode the CLI itself is blocked.** The permission
classifier denies `npx -y skills@latest add …` outright (hit 2026-09-04).
Hand-install is then the working route, and it is enough — the files plus the two
symlinks are all a harness needs:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills/NAME
cp REPO/CAT/NAME/SKILL.md ~/.agents/skills/NAME/
cp -R REPO/CAT/NAME/scripts REPO/CAT/NAME/agents ~/.agents/skills/NAME/   # when present
chmod +x ~/.agents/skills/NAME/scripts/*.sh
ln -s ../../.agents/skills/NAME ~/.claude/skills/NAME
ln -s ~/.claude/skills/NAME ~/.codex/skills/NAME
```

Copy `agents/openai.yaml` too whenever the skill ships one — it is the
Codex-facing manifest, and dropping it leaves Codex with a half install.

**Trap: never put `rm -rf` in the install script.** The `dcg` PreToolUse guard
blocks the *entire* command on rule `core.filesystem:rm-rf-general`, even when the
target is a subfolder you just created yourself. Copy only what you want instead of
copy-then-delete. `dcg` also false-positives on a `>` inside a heredoc'd Python
script (rule `core.filesystem:redirect-truncate-root-home`) — use the Edit tool for
that write rather than fighting the pattern.

**Trap: a hand-install is invisible to the ledger.** It gets no entry in
`~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`, so `skills update` will never touch it.
`skillFolderHash` is not a plain sha1 of the files and is not worth
reverse-engineering — have Eric run the official `add` command himself behind a `!`
prefix to register it.

**Trap: `-a` will not take a comma-separated list.** `-a claude-code,codex`
fails with "Invalid agents: claude-code,codex" and then prints a valid-agent
list containing both names. Repeat the flag instead.

**Trap: the installer does not always wire Codex.** It reports
`universal: Codex` and creates no symlink. Check
`ls -l ~/.codex/skills/<name>` after every install and make the symlink by hand
if it is missing.

The CLI runs a security scan and may report alerts. Read
`https://skills.sh/<owner>/<repo>` before trusting a skill.

**Cowork cannot take a locally-dropped skill.** Its store is
`~/Library/Application Support/Claude/local-agent-mode-sessions/skills-plugin/<a>/<b>/skills/`
with a sibling `manifest.json`, and every entry carries a **server-minted id**
(`skill_01…`). A folder placed there is not in the manifest and is wiped on the
next sync. The only route is a zip uploaded through claude.ai → Settings →
Capabilities → Skills, with the skill folder at the zip root. Expect Cowork's
sandbox to lack ffmpeg/Chrome, so any skill's verification or media step will
not run there even after a successful upload.

Where a skill puts its *output* is separate: some resolve a workspace from the
nearest `.git` walking up, so run them from inside the target project or set
their env override, or builds land wherever cwd happened to be.

See [[vendored-skill-repair]] for what to do when one of these is broken, and
[[path-shadowing-and-cleanup]] before deleting any copy.

When a third-party skill produces **empty output rather than an error**, suspect
a CLI flag the underlying tool has since removed, not the skill's own logic.

**The instance (2026-09-02):** `/watch` returned zero frames with no useful
message. Cause: `frames.py` passed ffmpeg `-vsync`, removed in ffmpeg 7+. This
machine runs **ffmpeg 9.0.1**. Fix is `-vsync` → `-fps_mode` (same `vfr` value,
same position, exists since ffmpeg 5.0).

**Patch every live copy, and know which ones matter.** A skill can exist three
times on this machine:

1. `~/.agents/skills/<name>/…` — the vendor store, serves `~/.claude/skills/` and Codex.
2. `~/.claude/plugins/cache/<plugin>/<skill>/<version>/skills/<name>/…` — the
   plugin copy. **This is the one a `/slash` invocation actually loads.** Patch
   only the vendor store and the skill stays broken.
3. The Cowork copy under `Library/Application Support/Claude/…` — **do not
   patch.** It is server-synced and reverts. See [[vendored-skill-install]].

Confirm which file is live by reading the "Base directory for this skill" line
the harness prints when the skill loads.

**Every such patch is temporary.** Check upstream before assuming a fix is
needed, and after patching, assume `skills update` or a plugin update reinstalls
the bug. For `/watch` the upstream is `bradautomates/claude-video`, still
carrying `-vsync` as of its 2026-06-30 commit.

Verify by running the affected code path and **counting the output**, not by
reading the exit code — the original failure exited 0.

### DEV/project_zsh-shell-traps.md

---
name: zsh-shell-traps
description: "zsh-specific shell traps hit repeatedly on this macOS machine — path/UID/status reserved variables, word-splitting"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: a86cfb00-e6d1-46b9-8cdc-35e21acd9931
  modified: 2026-08-07T00:53:25.947Z
---

zsh quirks that have repeatedly broken scripts in Claude sessions on this machine:

- **Never use `path` as a variable name** — zsh ties lowercase `path` (array) to `PATH`; assigning it a scalar clobbers PATH mid-script ("command not found" for everything after).
- `UID` and `status` are read-only in zsh — use `ZUID`, `st`, etc.
- Unquoted `$VAR` does NOT word-split in zsh — use `${=VAR}` when splitting is intended.
- Background-task shells get a minimal PATH; start scripts with `export PATH="/usr/bin:/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH"` and use `$HOME/go/bin` for Go CLIs.
- `head` at the end of a pipeline masks grep's exit code — use `grep -q` for presence tests, never `grep -l ... | head && echo FOUND`.
- **git fetch/push/pull to private repos hangs silently** in sandboxed/background shells — no keychain access means git blocks on an invisible credential prompt (looks exactly like a network outage; `ls-remote` on public paths still works). Fix: `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 git -c credential.helper= -c 'credential.helper=!gh auth git-credential' <cmd>`.

**Why:** each cost a debugging round in the Aug 2026 restore/printing sessions.
**How to apply:** prefer these idioms proactively in any zsh/bash-on-macOS scripting here.

Eric's limiting factor on deep work is environmental, not motivational. He is highly productive in short bursts once work actually starts; what breaks is the path to starting. The specific disruptor he named (2026-07-28) is the pull to share what he's working on — with no standing outlet for it, he goes and finds people, which costs him the session.

**Corrected 2026-07-29.** The pull toward people is not a leak, it's the generative stage. His own observation: alone he wants company; in company the project ideas arrive. Solitude is where he refines, not where he generates. A long unbroken solo block with nothing in the hopper is waiting, not deep work.

**Second brake, same day:** he holds ideas back from fear of overstepping into others' lanes, against an unstated expectation that he act unasked. He is deliberately moving off this position ("if I don't act, ideas wither"). Pressfield's Resistance is his frame for it.

**Qualified 2026-08-03.** The permission gate is not entirely self-imposed. He acted unasked on a device another staffer was already championing (ShiftWave chair, second trial unit) and took real organizational blowback for it — careful, low-key handling bought nothing, because the claim was made by initiating, not by presenting. So the caution is warranted on ground someone has visibly attached themselves to, and unwarranted everywhere else. His same-day reaction ("pander to the people in power, keep your head down") is a bruise, not necessarily a settled position — don't treat it as one.

**Why:** Both reframe what looks like procrastination. The first is an unmet structural need (input/ideation) improvising in real time; the second is a self-imposed permission gate that reads as professional courtesy. Neither is a discipline failure, and treating them as one produces useless advice.

**How to apply:** Act as the thinking partner in-session — reflect his reasoning back, name what's interesting in it, and give him something to react to rather than only executing tasks silently. When he's ideating, don't rush to implementation; the ideation *is* the need being met, and it's the stage that feeds everything else — help him capture what surfaces. Prefer short, well-scoped blocks with a clear starting line. When he hesitates on whether something is his to do, first ask whether anyone has visibly claimed it — if not, name the permission gate rather than validating the caution; if someone has, the hesitation is a correct read and the useful move is how to approach the owner, not encouragement to proceed. Related: [[company-generates-solitude-refines]], [[waiting-for-the-ask-kills-the-idea]], [[ownership-not-merit-governs-the-reaction]], [[design-the-conditions-not-the-discipline]] in the SecondBrain vault.


## Instructions

Look for:
- Direct contradictions (one file says X, another says not-X)
- The same fact stated in two files, where one is more current than the other
- Statements that name a path, tool, schedule or version that another file says has moved,
  been retired, or been replaced
- Advice in one file that a later file's experience overturns

For each issue found, output EXACTLY one line in this format:
CONTRADICTION: [file1] vs [file2] - description of the conflict
REDUNDANT: [file1] vs [file2] - what is duplicated and which looks newer
STALE: [file] - what it asserts and what supersedes it

If no issues found, output exactly: NO_ISSUES

Do NOT output anything else - no preamble, no explanation, just the formatted lines.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead. Based on Wikipedia's comprehensive "Signs of AI writing" guide. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. - skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. - xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.

# Machine

Machine-specific shell, paths, and traps live in `~/.claude/machine.md` (gitignored; copy `machine.macos.md` or `machine.windows.md` to `machine.md` on a new machine). It is imported below.

@machine.md

Two machines share this setup: the MacBook (`~/DEV`) and the Baylor Windows laptop (`~/Desktop/DEV`). Projects sync through GitHub (`erash11`), documents through Google Drive. Every project repo carries a Session routine in its `AGENTS.md`: `git pull` + read `docs/STATUS.md` at start; update `STATUS.md`, commit, `git push` at end.
# Workflow Expectations

- When asked to **create, merge, or consolidate an artifact** (calendar, deck, doc), the expected deliverable is always a produced file. Verify what exists first, then create the artifact regardless — never conclude with "it already exists" instead of delivering the file.
- When the user types `/graphify`, invoke the Skill tool with `skill: "graphify"` before doing anything else.

# Session Startup

Handled by the `keystone-unified-snapshot.js` SessionStart hook — do not read these files by hand. It injects `global-memory/USER.md`, `global-memory/MEMORY.md`, `transcripts/.errors.log` (only when non-empty), and a pointer to the KeystoneOS snapshot.

- If `.errors.log` content appears, surface it once on the first response, then continue. It is normally empty; entries mean hook failures.
- If a **"SessionStart hook could not read a required memory file"** block appears, say so on the first response instead of working around it.
- **If no `## User profile` block is in context at session start, the hook did not fire.** Say so, then read `USER.md`, `MEMORY.md` and `transcripts/.errors.log` by hand.
- What the hook injects is a frozen snapshot. Mid-session writes take effect next session. Never load more than this proactively.

# Memory — routing only

The two-tier memory system (`~/.claude/global-memory/` and `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`) is owned by the **`memory-write` skill**, which holds the tier rules, character caps, slug rules, write steps, retrieval ladder, and daily-compiled-log rules.

The active project's Tier A memory (`~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`, indexed by its `MEMORY.md`) is **auto-injected by the harness** each session. Tier A files are also indexed by memsearch, so they stay recallable across projects.

- Writing a fact — "remember this", "note that", "save this", "forget about" → `Skill("memory-write")`
- Recalling past context — "did we already…?", "what did we decide about X" → `Skill("memory-write")`, retrieval-ladder section
- Daily compiled logs at `~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/daily/` are owned by `claude-memory-compiler`. Never hand-edit them; never read them eagerly.
- **Slugs differ per machine** (Mac `-Users-kristinarash-DEV-<X>`, Windows `C--Users-eric-rash-Desktop-DEV-<X>`). Tier A written on one is not auto-injected on the other; memsearch still finds it. Durable project facts belong in the repo's `docs/` so both machines see them.
